records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.save_figure_dialog#2
records.source: The dialog offers what belongs to the FILE -- its background, the colour and width of its lines, the colour of its text, the shape of its page, and what kind of file it is. Everything else a figure can be told belongs to the PLOT and lives on the plot's own right-click menu, where it reaches the screen and every export at once; a value inherited from there is shown here rather than offered a second time. Matplotlib figures also have a live figure-settings menu. This dialog additionally offers an export-only text scale for the detached Matplotlib copy when the output page is resized.

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.save_figure_dialog.style_for_file#2
records.source: figure : matplotlib.figure.Figure or None Figure copy to modify. ``None`` is accepted for preview fallbacks. ink : str, optional Color applied to axes titles, axis labels, tick labels, legend entries, axes text, spines, and tick marks. Figure-level text, legend titles, and plotted data lines are unchanged. An empty string preserves the existing colors. text_colour : str, optional Color for the axes text elements listed under ``ink``. Overrides ``ink`` for those elements. line_colour : str, optional Color for LINES only: the spines and the tick marks. Overrides ``ink`` for that half. background : str, optional Figure and axes background color. An empty string makes both backgrounds transparent. grid : bool or None, default None Draw major grid lines when ``True`` and disable them when ``False``. ``None`` leaves the figure's own grid alone, which is what a caller with no grid control of its own wants: a default of ``False`` turns off a grid the figure was drawn with and nobody asked about. width, height : float, default 0 Output dimensions in inches. The size changes only when both values are positive. dpi : int, default 0 Output resolution. Zero preserves the figure's current resolution. font_scale : float, default 0 Multiplier applied to every text artist. Values at or below zero preserve the current text sizes.

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.save_figure_dialog.SaveFigureDialog#5
records.source: WHAT IT OFFERS, AND WHY IT IS SHORT. For a fast plot, four setting groups change how the FILE looks -- the background, the lines' colour and width, the text colour, and the shape of the page -- and three more say what the file IS: its format, resolution and page size. Everything else belongs on the plot's own right-click menu, where it applies to the screen and every export at once. Matplotlib figures also have a live figure-settings menu; this dialog provides an additional text scale for the export copy.
